seed: Objects of type `player` under action ACTION4 with touching neighbours [wall] show mixed outcomes: x x2, no_change x2. Find the condition in the before state that decides the outcome. Start from this kind of condition: a field of the object itself, such as its tags, pixels, visibility or layer. Verify it against every transition before you keep it.

synth.notes:
Block mode: ACTION1/2 move both cyan blocks up/down 4; ACTION3/4 move them apart/together (mirrored). Each block is blocked on its own by a hidden maze cell {(14,38),(6,18),(38,14)} or a marker cell (marker pos - 1).
Hypothesis result: the ACTION4 x vs no_change outcome depends on the target cell (maze or marker), not on any field of the player. The wall contact is irrelevant.
Clicking a marker arms the blocks (they become color_1 players) and activates that marker. ACTION1-4 then move the active marker by 4 with the same blocking. Clicking another marker switches; clicking the active one does nothing; clicking a player goes back to block mode.
Every action adds 1 to a hidden count n, kept only while the state matches the last one returned. The wall_0 bars are floor(3(n+1)/7) wide. Without that state, n is the smallest value that fits the bar width. Names are type_color_rank sorted by (y,x).
Not confirmed: board bounds (2..58 assumed) and ACTION7 (never observed, treated as no-op).
